script.base: No spread or total is in the pack, so the script is inferred from weeks 2-4 usage, not from a market number. Minnesota is a Jones run offense: Aaron Jones 60 carries and 257 yards (20.0 carries and 85.7 rush yards per game, 4.28 YPC), with D. Claiborne 6/13, Kyler Murray 5/38 and C. Wentz 3/6. The pass tree in that window is T.J. Hockenson 21 targets/159 yards/159 air, Jordan Addison 20/163/245, Aaron Jones 14/68/-5, Justin Jefferson only 8/87/109, then M. Price, Tai Felton and Jauan Jennings at 3 targets each. New Orleans is pass-first and run-poor: Chris Olave 35/309/414, DeVaughn Vele 22/157/253, Juwan Johnson 20/178/85, Alvin Kamara 14/47/5 receiving, while the rush committee is Kamara 25/74 (2.96 YPC), T. Etienne 21/82, Tyler Shough 11/65 and Kendre Miller 10/23. Base flow: MIN hands Jones the ball into a NO run defense allowing 5.27 YPC and 15 runs of 10+, with LBs Kaden Elliss and Anfernee Jennings already out; NO cannot lean on Kamara, so Shough keeps throwing, but MIN blitzes 73% and NO EPA/db is -0.18 when blitzed versus +0.12 when not, which should pull those throws short to Johnson rather than deep to Olave (11.8 aDOT) and Vele (11.5 aDOT). Who leads is unknown without a spread.
script.flip1: New Orleans scores early through Olave or Vele, especially if S Julian Blackmon (shoulder, questionable) is inactive and the deep middle opens. Minnesota then trails, abandons the 20-carry Jones plan, and Murray has to throw into an offense that is negative EPA both versus the blitz (-0.11) and clean (-0.05). Jones rush yards stall the way a trail script always stalls a workhorse, and a NO lead can also become a Kamara/Etienne clock-grind that cuts Juwan Johnson's second-half routes.
script.flip2: The MIN tackle group does not hold: Christian Darrisaw is out (concussion) and Brian O'Neill is questionable (knee), with C Michael Jurgens also questionable (elbow). Rush efficiency falls, MIN cannot stay on schedule, and if Jefferson (ankle) and Addison (hamstring) are limited the whole offense stalls. NO, already -0.18 EPA/db against the blitz, cannot punish it. Both the Jones rush over and the Johnson receiving over miss in a low-play slog.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting, so MOFO versus MOFC and man versus zone rate are unknown for both MIN and NO. Location YPA is the only shell proxy. NO defense, 4 games: left 7.86 YPA on 51 attempts, middle 9.17 on 23, right 6.25 on 48. Middle is the soft NO zone on a small sample; right is the strength. MIN defense, 4 games: left 6.75 on 44, middle 9.69 on 29, right 5.32 on 57. MIN also bleeds the middle and is strongest to the right, which is the wrong side of the field for a short middle tight end and the right side of the field to fade an outside deep receiver if he lives there.
matchup.pressure: NO blitz rate is 35%. Minnesota EPA per dropback is -0.11 against the blitz and -0.05 with no blitz, so NO pressure is a small problem for Murray, not a collapse, and it does not by itself force a checkdown game. MIN blitz rate is 73%. New Orleans EPA per dropback is -0.18 when blitzed and +0.12 when not blitzed. That split is the game lever: if MIN actually gets the blitz home, NO's efficient look disappears. Pressure-got-home rate and time-to-throw are not in the pack, so the EPA split is the evidence, not a charted pressure rate.
matchup.bleeds: NO run defense is the bleed: 5.27 yards per carry allowed, 15 runs of 10+, and the linebackers who would fit that run (Elliss, A. Jennings) are out, Ford questionable. MIN run defense is the opposite: 4.15 YPC allowed and 11 runs of 10+, which is a bad spot for Kamara at 2.96 YPC and Miller at 2.3 YPC. Through the air, both defenses bleed the middle (NO 9.17 YPA on 23, MIN 9.69 YPA on 29) and both have allowed explosives (NO 11 passes of 20+ for 130 yards, MIN 12 for 146). MIN's right-side 5.32 YPA is the coverage strength; NO's right-side 6.25 is better than its middle but still not a shutdown number.
matchup.overlap: The core overlap on the MIN side is Aaron Jones, the primary ballcarrier at 60 of the listed rushes, running into the exact place NO gives it up: 5.27 YPC, 15 explosive runs, and two linebackers out. The core overlap on the NO side is not the primary target. Olave leads the team with 35 targets and 414 air yards (11.8 aDOT) and Vele is next at 11.5 aDOT; those are deep profiles into a 73% blitz, not into MIN's middle bleed. Juwan Johnson is the overlap: 20 targets, only 85 air yards, 4.25 aDOT, 178 receiving yards, attacking the middle that MIN allows at 9.69 YPA, which is also where a heavy blitz is supposed to dump the ball.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both MIN@NO legs lost. Juwan Johnson: Minnesota's 73% blitz did not create easy middle targets, it wrecked the New Orleans dropback game, which is exactly what the -0.18 EPA per dropback versus the blitz warned. Tyler Shough never got Johnson the checkdowns, a Jones clock-control game cut the play count, and the 53-yard floor from 66, 53, 59 was three other defenses. The unnamed MIN middle defender took away the 9.69 YPA look, and there was no coverage chart to catch that before kickoff. Aaron Jones: Christian Darrisaw was inactive, Brian O'Neill and Michael Jurgens were limited, New Orleans stacked the box because Jefferson and Addison were not full threats, and something like 18 carries at 3.1 YPC finished near the 58-yard game instead of the 85.7 average. The 5.27 YPC allowed was other offensive lines, not this tackle group. Both legs also die together if New Orleans leads early: Jones is abandoned, and NO can hand the ball to Kamara and Etienne instead of feeding Johnson. No weather line was saved, so a wind or rain drag could not be checked, and a dome assumption was not used because the pack never states the venue.
slip_story: One MIN@NO story, not a shootout stack and not a mix of an under with same-game overs. Minnesota controls the ground through Aaron Jones, and New Orleans cannot run (Kamara 2.96 YPC, Etienne sharing the carries, Jeremiah Wright out), so Shough has to throw short into the blitz. Jones rushyds over 71.5 is the run-defense overlap. Johnson recyds over 42.5 is the blitz-to-tight-end overlap, explicitly not an Olave or Vele deep stack. They fit a competitive or Minnesota-leaning game. They do not fit a New Orleans blowout or a total offensive collapse from the tackle injuries. The correlated piece left off the card is Alvin Kamara rushyds under 32.5, mean 24.7 in the saved last-4, which belongs to the same story only if he is confirmed active. No bet is being placed.
